text.tspan: Figure 1 | Deep-learning mining of the gut microbiome identifies antimicrobial peptides that distinguish Alzheimer’s disease from healthy controls.
(a) Discovery workflow: faecal shotgun metagenomes from 62 patients with Alzheimer’s disease (AD) and 64 age- and sex-matched healthy controls (HC)

g.text: were assembled, screened for small open reading frames (smORFs, 30–300 bp) and classified with a bidirectional LSTM plus attention encoder; each dot is one participant. (b) Principal-coordinate analysis of Bray–Curtis dissimilarity with 95% confidence ellipses and marginal rugs for every subject.

(c) Receiver-operating characteristic with bootstrap 95% band, held-out confusion matrix and calibration curve. (d) Candidate AMP load per group shown as violin, box (median, IQR, 1.5× IQR whiskers) and all individual participants. (e) Volcano plot of all 2,349 candidate AMPs. (f) Row-scaled

abundance of the ten most discriminative peptides across 24 representative subjects with hierarchical clustering and correlated taxa. (g) Family enrichment as odds ratios with 95% confidence intervals, and family composition per group. (h) Schiffer–Edmundson projection, physicochemical properties,

and net charge versus hydrophobic moment for all candidates. (i) Membrane-disruption mechanism, minimum inhibitory concentrations and time-kill kinetics. (j) Rarefaction of unique peptide discovery. (k) Enriched sequence motif and length distribution. (l) Overlap with reference AMP databases and

peptide–taxon correlation network. Statistical tests are named in the corresponding panels; all P values are two-sided and corrected by the Benjamini–Hochberg procedure. Values shown are illustrative. Anatomical and molecular artwork adapted from Servier Medical Art and DBCLS via Bioicons
